title: Kathmandu Sightseeing Itinerary: 1 to 4 Day Plans
meta_description: Kathmandu sightseeing itinerary for 1, 2, 3 and 4 days, with the order we visit temples and Durbar Squares, drive times between them and current entry fees.
summary: One day in Kathmandu covers Swayambhunath, Kathmandu Durbar Square, Pashupatinath and Boudhanath. Two days add Patan and Bhaktapur, three days allow Changunarayan and a Nagarkot sunrise, and four days fit the Chandragiri cable car, Kirtipur or the Everest mountain flight. Plan 3–4 sites a day, because valley traffic turns 10 km into 45 minutes.

sections.heading: How we plan a Kathmandu sightseeing day
paras: The Kathmandu Valley is small, about 25 km across, but its roads are narrow and crowded, and distances on a map mislead first-time visitors. We plan around three rules. Start by 8 am, before school and office traffic peaks at 9–10 am. Group sites by side of the valley, so Pashupatinath and Boudhanath go together in the east, and Swayambhunath and Kathmandu Durbar Square together in the west. Keep each day to three or four major stops, with lunch near the third.

Each site in this plan needs 1–2 hours on foot with a guide. A licensed city guide explains the temples, handles tickets and finds the side lanes most visitors miss; expect about US$25–35 or ₹2,000–3,000 for a full day. A private car with driver for a full day in the valley costs roughly NPR 5,000–8,000 depending on the vehicle. The table shows typical drive times from Thamel at mid-morning; add 30–50 percent at rush hour.

sections.heading: One day in Kathmandu
paras: With only one day, we cover the four sites that define the valley, in an order that follows the traffic and ends at the best evening setting. This plan works well for travellers on a layover, pilgrims heading to Muktinath, or anyone who arrives the night before a trek.

Start at Swayambhunath at 8 am, when monks and local families walk the stupa and the light falls across the city from the hilltop. Drive 20 minutes to Kathmandu Durbar Square for 9:30 am to see Hanuman Dhoka, the Kasthamandap pavilion rebuilt after 2015, and the window of the Kumari Ghar. Walk north through Indra Chowk and Asan market to see spice and brass shops, then lunch in Thamel or Durbar Marg.

After lunch, drive 30–40 minutes east to Pashupatinath. Indian Hindus can enter the main temple for darshan; non-Hindus view it from the terraces across the Bagmati. Finish at Boudhanath from about 4:30 pm, when hundreds of people walk the kora clockwise around the stupa and butter lamps are lit. If you prefer the evening aarti at Pashupatinath, which starts around 6 pm (earlier in winter), swap the last two stops.

sections.heading: Two days: add Patan and Bhaktapur
paras: Two days let you see all three royal cities of the valley without rushing. We keep day one as above but finish at Boudhanath, and give day two to the old Newar towns south and east of Kathmandu.
list: Day 2, 8:30 am: drive 30–45 minutes to Patan Durbar Square; see Krishna Mandir, the Golden Temple (Hiranya Varna Mahavihar) and the Patan Museum, which opens mid-morning
Day 2, 12:30 pm: lunch in Patan, then drive about 50 minutes to Bhaktapur
Day 2, 2 pm: walk Bhaktapur Durbar Square, Taumadhi Square with the five-storey Nyatapola temple, and Pottery Square
Day 2, 5 pm: taste juju dhau, the local curd, and return to Kathmandu by 6:30 pm

sections.heading: Three days: Changunarayan and a Nagarkot sunrise
paras: With a third day, we slow Bhaktapur down and add the oldest temple in the valley. Day one stays in Kathmandu with Swayambhunath, Durbar Square and the Asan walk, finishing with Pashupatinath's evening aarti. Day two pairs Boudhanath in the morning with Patan in the afternoon, so neither site is squeezed.

On day three, drive to Bhaktapur for 8:30 am, before the tour groups arrive at 10, and spend three hours in its squares and courtyards. After lunch, drive 20–25 minutes to Changunarayan, a hilltop temple with a Licchavi inscription dated 464 CE and fine stone carvings. From there you can continue 45 minutes to Nagarkot (2,175 m) for sunset and an overnight stay, then watch sunrise over the Himalaya from the view tower before driving 1.5 hours back to Kathmandu. Guests who prefer their Kathmandu hotel can return the same evening.
Fit walkers can swap the drive for the Changunarayan to Bhaktapur walk, about 2.5 hours downhill through terraced fields, or walk from Nagarkot to Changunarayan in 4–5 hours the next morning.

sections.heading: Four days: Chandragiri, Kirtipur or a flight
paras: A fourth day in the valley opens four good options, and we choose based on the season and your energy after day three. The mountain flight and Chandragiri both depend on clear weather, so we keep them flexible and move them to whichever morning has the best forecast. Kirtipur and the Dhulikhel–Namobuddha loop work in any weather, including light monsoon rain.

The flight pairs well with Kirtipur on the same day: you are back from the airport by 8:30 am, rest, and spend the afternoon in Kirtipur's lanes with a Newari lunch of beaten rice, choila and bara. Chandragiri fills a morning, leaving the afternoon for shopping in Thamel or Patan's metalwork lanes.
list: Everest mountain flight: a 1-hour dawn flight from Kathmandu domestic terminal past Everest and the Khumbu peaks, back at the hotel for breakfast by 8:30 am; best from October to February

Chandragiri Hills: drive 45 minutes to Thankot and ride the 2.5 km cable car for 10–12 minutes to 2,551 m, with Himalayan views from Annapurna to Langtang on clear days and the Bhaleshwor Mahadev temple at the top
Kirtipur and Chobhar: a quiet hilltop Newar town 5 km southwest of Kathmandu with the Bagh Bhairab and Uma Maheshwar temples, followed by the Chobhar gorge and Adinath temple
Dhulikhel and Namobuddha: drive about 1.5 hours east for the Thrangu monastery and the tigress stupa, returning via Panauti's Indreshwar temple

sections.heading: Entry fees at the main sites
paras: Most sites charge foreigners a fee at the gate, and Indian nationals pay the lower SAARC rate on showing a passport or voter ID. Fees are collected in Nepali rupees, so carry cash. A Kathmandu Durbar Square ticket lasts one day unless you ask for an extended pass with your passport, and the Bhaktapur ticket can be extended for a week. Fees are revised every few years, so check current status before you travel.
A four-day plan with all of the sites below costs a foreign visitor about NPR 5,700 in entry fees plus the cable car; an Indian visitor pays roughly NPR 1,000–1,500 plus the cable car.

sections.heading: Practical tips for sightseeing days
paras: Small choices make Kathmandu days easier. We keep the following in mind for every guest, from first-time families to repeat travellers.
list: Wear shoes you can slip off quickly; you remove them at many temple entrances and at Boudhanath's monasteries
Walk clockwise around stupas and prayer wheels, and keep leather items away from inner shrines where signs ask
Carry NPR 100 and 50 notes for donations, shoe minders and small purchases
Saturdays are the Nepali weekend: offices close, temples and Durbar Squares are busier, and city traffic is lighter
Avoid a Bhaktapur visit on the main day of Bisket Jatra in mid-April unless you want festival crowds
Keep 30 minutes of slack before an evening flight; airport traffic on Ring Road can take an hour

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Kathmandu sightseeing?
faqs.a: Two to three days are enough for Kathmandu sightseeing. Two days cover the seven UNESCO monument zones except Changunarayan, at a steady pace. Three days add Changunarayan and a Nagarkot sunrise, and leave room for evening aarti at Pashupatinath. One day works for the four main sites only. A fourth day suits the Everest mountain flight, the Chandragiri cable car or Kirtipur.

faqs.q: Can I see Kathmandu in one day?
faqs.a: Yes, you can see the main sights of Kathmandu in one long day. Start at Swayambhunath at 8 am, continue to Kathmandu Durbar Square, have lunch, then visit Pashupatinath and finish at Boudhanath around sunset. That is roughly 25 km of driving and 5–6 hours on foot. Patan and Bhaktapur need a second day, as traffic makes adding them rushed.

faqs.q: What is the best order to visit Kathmandu temples?
faqs.a: Visit Swayambhunath first in the morning, then Kathmandu Durbar Square, both on the west side of the city. After lunch go east to Pashupatinath, then finish at Boudhanath 3 km away. This order follows the traffic, keeps Boudhanath for its busy evening kora, and lets you swap the last two stops if you want the Pashupatinath aarti around 6 pm.

faqs.q: How much are entry fees in Kathmandu for Indians?
faqs.a: Indian nationals pay the SAARC rate: about NPR 150 at Kathmandu Durbar Square, NPR 250 at Patan and NPR 500 at Bhaktapur, against NPR 1,000–1,800 for other foreigners. Hindu pilgrims enter Pashupatinath free for darshan, and Swayambhunath and Boudhanath cost very little. Show a passport or voter ID at the counter. Check current status before you travel, as fees change.

faqs.q: Is Bhaktapur worth visiting if I have seen Patan?
faqs.a: Yes. Bhaktapur feels different from Patan: it is quieter, has more car-free streets and keeps strong traditions such as pottery and wood carving. Taumadhi Square's five-storey Nyatapola temple, the 55-Window Palace and Pottery Square are unique to it. Plan at least three hours, arrive before 10 am to beat tour groups, and try juju dhau curd before you leave.

faqs.q: What time is the aarti at Pashupatinath?
faqs.a: The evening aarti at Pashupatinath takes place every day on the Bagmati ghats, starting around 6 pm in summer and about 5:30 pm in winter. It lasts roughly an hour with lamps, bells and bhajans. Arrive 30 minutes early for a step on the eastern bank facing the ghats. Saturdays and Mondays draw larger crowds, and on festival days police may restrict access.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for Kathmandu sightseeing?
faqs.a: A guide is not compulsory, but we recommend one for your first day. A licensed guide explains the temples, handles tickets and steers you to courtyards and shrines that are easy to miss. Full-day guides cost about US$25–35 or ₹2,000–3,000. Hire only licensed guides through your hotel or agency, and avoid unofficial guides who approach you at Durbar Square gates.

faqs.q: Can I combine Nagarkot with Kathmandu sightseeing?
faqs.a: Yes. Nagarkot is 32 km from Kathmandu, about 1.5 hours by road, and fits neatly after Bhaktapur and Changunarayan. Drive up in the afternoon, stay overnight at 2,175 m and watch sunrise over the Himalaya, then return to Kathmandu by 10 am. Clear views are most likely from October to February. Bring a warm layer, as dawn can be close to freezing in winter.

faqs.q: Is the Chandragiri cable car worth it?
faqs.a: Yes, on a clear day. The 2.5 km cable car from Thankot rises to 2,551 m in about 12 minutes, and the summit shows the Himalaya from Annapurna to Langtang and the whole valley below. The return fare is about US$23 for foreigners and around NPR 1,320 for SAARC visitors. Go early, before cloud builds, and check current status before you travel.
